metadata.title: Density Pass 26 -- East Cavalry Field: Stuart vs Custer (Ticks 505-560)
metadata.description: The simultaneous cavalry battle three miles east of Gettysburg while Pickett's Charge unfolds. Stuart's 4 brigades attempting to reach the Baltimore Pike and strike Meade's rear. Gregg and Custer blocking the way. Custer's charge -- 'Come on, you Wolverines!' -- that stops Stuart cold. One of the war's great cavalry actions, usually overlooked.

placements.notes: Stuart's 4 brigades at East Cavalry Field -- ordered by Lee to get behind Meade and strike when Pickett charges
Wade Hampton's brigade -- Stuart's finest. Riding southeast toward the Baltimore Pike.
Fitz Lee's brigade
Chambliss's brigade
Jenkins's brigade
Custer's Michigan brigade -- 23-year-old Brigadier General George Custer. He is about to save the battle.
Gregg's division -- positioned to block Stuart's advance
Hampton's brigade advancing -- Confederate cavalry in column heading for the Baltimore Pike
Custer deploying his Michigan men -- they are outnumbered 3.5 to 1
Gregg's division in line -- Gregg has placed himself squarely in Stuart's path
Hampton's charge -- the Confederate cavalry sweeping forward in a massive column
Fitz Lee following Hampton's charge
CUSTER'S CHARGE -- 7th Michigan at full gallop into Hampton's column. Come on you Wolverines!
Gregg's troopers joining the melee -- the collision of two cavalry forces at full speed
Hampton repulsed -- Custer has stopped the charge. Hampton wounded.
Fitz Lee falling back
Custer's Wolverines holding their ground -- Stuart cannot get through
Stuart's corps reforming -- Pickett's Charge is already failing. There is no rear to strike.
Gregg's division holding East Cavalry Field -- Stuart will not pass today
Stuart withdrawing -- Pickett has been repulsed. There is nothing left to support.
Custer's brigade -- they have stopped Stuart cold. 23 years old. He will remember this day.
